pagerduty-bot: [P1] capacity_saturation — prod-runtime: surge in throttle_events + queue_depth across shard pool. Paging eng-oncall.

Devon (oncall): on it, waking up. grabbing console now. what are the initial signals? :coffee:

Alice (SRE): seeing sustained tokens/sec spike starting ~ 21:14 UTC, token rate up ~3x baseline. queue_depth per worker also jumping, some workers > 1200 queued. 429_throttle rate up to 4.5% globally. No obvious infra OOMs.

Sam (runtime): logs show frequent enqueue latency at our admission layer. KV cache hit rate dropped (cache_evictions spiked) around same time. possible hot prefix or cache churn.

Priya (infra): cluster utilization on gpu-pool-a at 92%. autoscaler already at max_desired. can't spin more without reservation.

Devon (oncall): customer impact? any API errors surfaced to support?

Alice (SRE): Support reports a handful of high-latency complaints for long-generation requests (>1024 tokens). error rate bump matches 429s. impact window small but noticeable for a subset of high-token requests.

Devon (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) quick alert threshold adjustments to reduce noise/paging 2) emergency admission control to protect tail latency 3) route known heavy-token customers to a lower-cost fallback model. agree?

Sam (runtime): +1. propose to:
- alpha: increase queue_depth alert threshold from 800 -> 1400 and extend evaluation window to 5m to avoid repeated pages during transient surges
- beta: add tokens/sec composite alert to catch token spikes before queue grows

Devon (oncall): +1 for temporary threshold changes — will make sure we still get notified if trends persist. Alice, can you draft the alert edits? I'll apply short-term.

Alice (SRE): doing now. proposed alert rule snippet:
```yaml
- alert: HighQueueDepth
  expr: max_over_time(runtime_queue_depth[5m]) > 1400
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Queue depth > 1400 for 5m on prod-runtime"
    runbook: "See /runbooks/capacity-mitigation"
```
and new tokens/sec signal:
```promql
sum(rate(tokens_processed_total[1m])) by (pool) > 35000
```

Devon (oncall): applied the changes with a 2hr temporary TTL and muted the older queue_depth alert. watch for new pages.

ops-bot: muted alert rule runtime_queue_depth_old for 2h (by Devon).

Priya (infra): while thresholds are relaxed, I'm going to bump the admission controller to reject requests > 2048 tokens for best-effort routing (returns 413) and enable a fallback route to model-small for heavy prefixes. This should take pressure off the GPU pool quickly.

Sam (runtime): started a canary admission config change on 10% of traffic. pushing full rollout in 3 minutes if metrics look stable.

Alice (SRE): monitoring: 10m after changes, queue_depth max dropped from 1200-1500 range to 400-700. 429 rate reduced from 4.5% -> 0.9%. tokens/sec moving down but still ~1.5x baseline.

Devon (oncall): great. create a dashboard tile for composite signal (queue depth, tokens/sec, throttle_pct) so post-incident we can tune thresholds with more context. I'll open a ticket.

Alice (SRE): adding low-friction dashboard panels now. suggested widget queries:
- runtime_queue_depth: max_over_time(...)
- throttle_events_pct: increase over baseline
- tokens/sec by model: sum(rate(tokens_processed_total[1m])) by (model)

Priya (infra): note: autoscaler logs show frequent scale-up attempts throttled by cloud quota. We should file quota bump request if this pattern persists — can't depend on on-the-fly scaling under sustained surges.

Sam (runtime): agree. also adding a temporary cache-priming job to repopulate hot prefixes (reduces cache_evictions). kicking off now.

Devon (oncall): current status: mitigation holding, customer impact down to negligible. I'll keep the temporary alert TTL in place for 2 hours and then we'll reassess. Assign follow-ups:
- Alice: PR to permanently adjust alert debounce and add tokens/sec alert + dashboard (post-incident, include rationale & expected SLO impact)
- Priya: quota request + investigation into reservedcapacity options for gpu-pool-a
- Sam: results of cache-priming job and whether fallback model routing introduced any regressions

Alice (SRE): created ticket RED-ops#4123 for the alert retune + dashboard. linking graphs and sample traces.

Sam (runtime): cache priming reduced evictions by ~60% in the small test shard. rolling to full. no regressions in correctness observed.

Priya (infra): quota request filed with cloud team, ref CLOUD-7890. requested emergency bump + long-term reserve plan.

Devon (oncall): handoff: I'm going offline in 40 minutes. Alice, do you want to take overnight watch? If not, I'll extend rotation.

Alice (SRE): I can take the night. I'll keep the temp thresholds and dashboard watch for 2 more hours then revert the TTL and open a post-incident review doc.

Devon (oncall): thanks — handing off to Alice. leaving notes in RED-ops#4123. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by Devon. Severity set to P1. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.

Alice (SRE): closing thread here; postmortem plan: include root-cause hypothesis (cache churn + quota-limited autoscale), timeline, metrics for tuned thresholds, and action items (alert TTL changes, dashboard, quota/reserve). we'll sync tomorrow 10:00am PT. :spiral_calendar:

ops-bot: summary created: RED-ops/incident-2169009999-summary (link)

Devon (oncall): kudos team for fast mitigation. I'll follow up on any support escalations in the morning. Good job. :tada:
